title: Diagonal Traversal of a Binary Tree
statement:
You are given a binary tree. Print its **diagonal traversal**.

Assign every node a **diagonal index**: the root has index `0`; a **left** child has the **same** index as its parent; a **right** child has index **parent's index + 1**. All nodes with the same diagonal index form one diagonal.

Print the diagonals in increasing order of index, one diagonal per line. Inside a diagonal, list the nodes in **level order**: nodes closer to the root first, and nodes at the same depth from left to right.

For example, take the tree whose root `1` has children `2` (left) and `3` (right), where `2` has children `4` and `5`, and `3` has children `7` and `6` (left to right). The diagonals are `1 2 4`, then `3 5 7`, then `6`.
inputFormat: A single line (or several lines) with the tree in level order, values separated by spaces, using `null` for a missing child. As in the usual level-order serialization, children of `null` nodes are not listed and trailing `null` values may be omitted. The first token is the root and is never `null`.
outputFormat: Print one line per diagonal, in increasing diagonal index. Each line contains the node values of that diagonal separated by single spaces.
constraints: The height of the tree is at most 5000

examples.explanation: Index 0: nodes 1, 2, 4 (following left children from the root). Index 1: 3 (right child of 1), 5 (right child of 2) and 7 (left child of 3); in level order they read 3, 5, 7. Index 2: 6 (right child of 3).
The tree is a chain of right children, so each node starts a new diagonal.
Index 0: 10 and its left child -2. Index 1: 7 (right of 10), then at depth 2 the node 4 (right of -2) and 3 (left of 7), left to right.

tests.input: 13 23 null -14 -30 -49 null null null 39 null null 36

hints: Walking down from a node, going left keeps you on the same diagonal and going right moves you to the next one. Track a diagonal index for each node.
A breadth-first traversal visits nodes in exactly the order required inside each diagonal (shallower first, then left to right). Carry (node, diagonal index) in the queue.
Append each visited node to a list for its diagonal index, then print the lists in order of index.
